title: Claude forgets. I measured how much

scenes.narration: In my long Claude Code sessions, Claude forgets what I asked for at the start. So I measured how much.
When a session gets too long, Claude Code replaces it with a summary, then summarises the summary. Of seventy-two early facts, only one in ten survived intact.
So I built Cogi. It's plain search, not a new kind of memory. It keeps every message word for word on my laptop, with no AI call to save.
When Claude needs something, it gets back one page of my own words. On my sessions, that page fully answered about three in four questions.
In a public test with over a million tokens of history, it put the right past chat in its top five, ninety-three percent of the time.
And one page answered almost as well as rereading the whole conversation, from nine times less text.
It works best when Claude searches on purpose. The full story, with every test and its limits, is on my blog.
